summary: Oakville's wooden lighthouse of 1888-89 was moved in 1960 to the Oakville Yacht Squadron grounds; a working light stands on the east pier.

light.note: Current light on the south end of the east pier (Coast Guard List of Lights, entry 528). Seasonal. LighthouseFriends describes it as a flashing red light.

structures.note: 36 ft (LighthouseFriends); foundation begun August 22, 1837; completed November 1, 1838

structures.type: hexagonal wooden tower, three stories, shingled, with an iron lantern
structures.note: Built by Henry George of Port Elgin for $960; by-law and OYS give 1889; LighthouseFriends gives operation on June 4, 1888

structures.type: white cylindrical tower with red upper portion
structures.note: Current working light on the east pier (Coast Guard list)

staffing.note: Keepers listed from 1866 to at least 1940 (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: The old lighthouse stands on the grounds of the Oakville Yacht Squadron, a private club. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. Doors Open Ontario has listed it in past years, but it was not in the current season's program.

facts.agency: Oakville Yacht Squadron (old lighthouse); Canadian Coast Guard (working light)

events.note: Work began in August 1837 (LighthouseFriends); the by-law says the first lighthouse was built in 1837
Completed November 1, 1838, per the commissioners' report as LighthouseFriends quotes it; OYS gives 1836 for the first light
Easterly storm in April destroyed the east pier and the light (LighthouseFriends quoting the Department of Marine report: 7 April; by-law: 8 April)
Hexagonal wooden tower placed in operation June 4, 1888 (LighthouseFriends). The by-law and OYS date the replacement to 1889 (construction began April 2; first lit June 4).
Moved 60 feet shoreward after pier damage (LighthouseFriends)
Fire damaged the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends, from photographs)
Fire damaged the lighthouse again (LighthouseFriends, from photographs)
Works table for fiscal 1922-23 lists 'Repairs to tower' at Oakville
Storm washed away the wooden pier and left the light on an island (by-law; OYS)
Replaced by a modern steel (OYS) or cylindrical cement (LighthouseFriends) structure; the old lighthouse saved and moved to the OYS grounds
Reopened by Mayor William Anderson on June 19, 1963 after rebuilding costing over $11,000 (OYS)
Refurbished in 1990, 2007, 2012 and 2013 by OYS members (OYS)

Designated by Town of Oakville By-law 1991-162 under the Ontario Heritage Act, passed in July 1991 (cover letter July 24, 1991). OYS says it was declared a Heritage Structure on January 9, 1991, about six months earlier; the sources do not explain the difference. See notes_for_editor.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends quotes the commissioners' report: the foundation was begun on 22 August 1837 and the light was completed on 1 November 1838, 'and has, since that time, been regularly lighted'. The 1837 date is the start of work (and the by-law's 'built'), not the first lighting. Human check: the by-law gives 1837 as the build date.

corrections.proposed: hexagonal wooden tower, built 1888 or 1889 (sources differ), on the grounds of the Oakville Yacht Squadron since 1960
corrections.why: The record gives one date; the sources disagree between June 4, 1888 (LighthouseFriends) and 1889 (by-law, OYS, Doors Open Ontario).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The by-law's 1837 is the start of construction and LighthouseFriends' 1838 is the completion; both fit the same first light. The OYS page's 1836 is not supported by the commissioners' report as LighthouseFriends quotes it.

notes_for_editor: 1) Dates disagree: first light 1836 (OYS), 1837 (by-law), 1838 completed (LighthouseFriends). Second light: June 4, 1888 (LighthouseFriends) or 1889 (by-law, OYS, Doors Open). The story gives both. 2) Storm: 7 April 1886 (LighthouseFriends quoting the Marine report) or 8 April (by-law). 3) Contractor: 'John George' at $937 in 1887 (LighthouseFriends) or 'Henry George' at $960 (by-law, OYS, Doors Open). 4) Currency: LighthouseFriends writes pounds, and the cached text garbles the pound sign; OYS writes $852. The story gives no amount for the first light. 5) The by-law quotes a diarist identified only as 'Summer'; I did not identify him, and the story says so. 6) Designation: the by-law's passage line is garbled at the day, but reads July 1991; its cover letter is dated July 24, 1991. OYS says the club's lighthouse was declared a Heritage Structure on January 9, 1991, about six months before the by-law. The story gives both and says the sources do not explain the difference. 7) The 1920 and 1922 fire damage rests on LighthouseFriends' note about photographs; I did not check the Marine reports for those years. 8) Keepers: Robert Kerr Chisholm (LighthouseFriends; the DCB names him postmaster and customs collector, not keeper). Maurice Felan: the Marine list for fiscal 1902 (Oakville Pier) and later keeper tables support him. Frank McCraney appears only in LighthouseFriends. 9) The Marine reports before 1900 are not in the corpus, so the 1886 Department of Marine report is quoted through LighthouseFriends only. 10) LighthouseFriends calls the present light 'flashing red'; the Coast Guard list gives Iso R 2s (isophase red). The story uses the Coast Guard's words. 11) The club's page calls the 1960 replacement 'a modern steel structure'; LighthouseFriends calls it 'a cylindrical cement tower'. Both are quoted or paraphrased as their sources say; the story now states the disagreement, and the working light is described from the Coast Guard list only (the opening no longer says it 'replaced' the old tower). 12) Access: a private club's grounds. Visiting arrangements not checked with the club. 13) Named people in public roles: Doug Armour (OYS's first commodore), Mayor William Anderson, William Chisholm (DCB), Robert Kerr Chisholm (LighthouseFriends; DCB). No one is named from after 1960 beyond public officers. 14) The 'Erchless' house and the Chisholm family's later members are left out. 15) Fixed in the 2026-10-28 check: the opening's 'two lights in one place' was wrong (the old tower is on the club grounds, not the pier) and is now 'two lighthouses'; LighthouseFriends says Chisholm paid for the overrun, not part of it; the Doors Open listing names Henry George as architect, not builder. 16) Page image not viewed: the image host for the 1902 lightkeeper list (scan p. 235) fails its TLS check from this machine. The 'Felan, Maurice Oakville Pier' pairing is one OCR row; the same name-and-station rows appear in the 1903, 1905, 1906, 1909 and 1911 keeper lists, which supports it, but the image itself was not read.
